instructions: At least 3 hours ahead, or the night before: mash the garlic and the salt together into a paste. Stir in the olive oil, the juice of 1 lemon and the sumac until it looks creamy.
Cut a few shallow slits into each thigh. Put the chicken and the garlic mixture in a zip-top bag and massage it in. Refrigerate for at least 3 hours, or overnight.
Set a 12-inch cast-iron skillet or grill pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes. Lift the thighs out of the bag and let the extra marinade drip off.
Lay the thighs in the pan, in two batches if they don't fit in one layer. Cook for 6 to 7 minutes, until the underside is deep brown and lets go of the pan.

Flip them and cook for 6 to 7 minutes. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece open: it's done when the juices run clear and there's no pink left.
Transfer the chicken to a board and rest it for 5 minutes. Cut the second lemon into wedges.
Taste a piece. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon. Serve with the lemon wedges.
advance_prep_notes: marinate at least 3 hours ahead, or overnight
method_notes: All the versions marinate the chicken in a paste of garlic, olive oil, lemon and sumac and cook it over medium heat until the juices run clear. Fas Kitchen (the lead) uses 6 garlic cloves, a 3 hour marinade and boneless pieces, Food.com cuts a whole chicken and marinates 3 to 6 hours, and Chef Soju adds paprika, cinnamon and cumin and a toum on the side. This version uses boneless thighs in a skillet so it fits a weeknight.
